basis: Inherited platelet dense-granule dysfunction causes bleeding; bruising does not establish primary skin disease.
Neuroendocrine tumor arising in the duodenum; somatostatin production alone does not establish an endocrine dysfunction syndrome.
Hereditary cerebellar degeneration defines this ataxia group; no other organ involvement is established across the group.
Substance-use disorder; specific toxic organ injuries are separate diagnoses and are not universal across substances.
Intrahepatic bile duct atresia; the unspecified syndromic designation does not establish additional affected organs.
Plasmodium malariae infects erythrocytes; associated nephropathy is a separate diagnosis and not common enough for inclusion.
Cognitive dysfunction is a defining component of this chronic multisymptom syndrome; pain, rash and respiratory symptoms do not establish common direct organ damage.
Familial transverse crease of the external nasal skin; no airway disease is established.
Secondary glaucoma damages the eye and optic nerve in individuals with aniridia.
Hyperplasia of the parathyroid endocrine gland; hyperparathyroid skeletal or renal disease is not established by this concept.
Carcinoma arising in the vulva, a reproductive organ outside the axes; HPV risk does not make the carcinoma an infection.
Inherited susceptibility to chronic Candida infection of skin, nails and oral mucosa; unspecified endocrine findings do not establish common endocrine disease.
Primary cutaneous T-cell lymphoma involves skin and lymphoid blood cells; lymphoma also receives the immune mechanism axis.
Cyclic neutrophil deficiency; intrinsic oral ulceration and gingivitis occur in 30-79%. Secondary skin and respiratory infections are separate diseases.
Persistent hiccup is an autonomic movement disorder; muscle contractions do not establish muscle damage, and nutritional consequences do not establish endocrine disease.
Congenital contractures and arthrogryposis occur in 3/3; reduced fetal movement and absent stomach bubble do not establish separate neural or intestinal damage.
Varicose mesenteric veins are a vascular disorder; their location does not establish intestinal disease.
Skeletal myopathy and severe external ophthalmoplegia define the disease; no independent peripheral nerve disorder is established.
Muscular dystrophy, contractures and joint hypermobility define it. Hypoventilation in 1/3 reflects respiratory muscle weakness, without established direct lung disease.
Congenital absence of a patent intestinal lumen directly affects the gastrointestinal tract.
Primary breast carcinoma lies outside the axes; neuroendocrine differentiation alone does not establish endocrine gland disease or hormonal dysfunction.
Absent or dysgenetic testes cause gonadal endocrine failure, with low testosterone, elevated gonadotropins and absent pubertal development.
Malignant tumor arising from peripheral nerve sheath; no common additional directly damaged organ is established.
Primary cutaneous lymphoma of mature T cells; skin origin, lymphoid blood-cell neoplasia and lymphoma mechanism define the axes.
Direct lesion of the sciatic peripheral nerve; secondary weakness does not establish a primary muscle disorder.
